newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Oil sideways as funds balance oversupply.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Oil sideways as funds balance oversupply.

text.p: Oil prices moved sideways on Monday as speculative buying balanced a sickly outlook for the key Atlantic Basin physical crude market.
London futures for benchmark May Brent at 1600 GMT stood unchanged at $19.70 a barrel after reaching a three-week high on Friday.
Dealers said buying interest from the investment funds which closely track commodity price trends continued to support the market.
But physical traders were taking a pessimistic view of the balance for supply and demand as spot market cargoes sold on Monday at growing discounts versus the futures market.

"There's certainly no shortage of crude supplies but the market hit an important area of support last week and we're still seeing some reaction from that mostly in the form of some fund buying," said a trader.
"The funds have taken the view that prices hit bottom and are on the way up again."
Brent slipped to $18.68 a barrel two weeks ago from just below $25 in mid-January.
Traders in the United States were looking for fresh signs of a revival for gasoline, which traditionally lends support to the oil complex in spring.
U.S. gasoline inventories are at a significant deficit to year-ago levels as the industry gears up for the spring and summer driving seasons.
Refinery profit margins in Europe and the United States recovered a little last week from recent lows but still remain at depressed levels.
But margins in Singapore, Asia's benchmark refining centre, soared to average $5.40 a barrel on a barrel of Middle East Dubai crude.
That has helped spark renewed buying interest from Asian refiners for West African crudes. China took a large cargo on Monday.
